answer:
Use the OpenFOAM solver interFoam for the simulation.
The simulation is transient and gravity-driven.
Set gravity to (0 -9.81 0).
The tank is a rectangular box with length 1.0 m in x, height 0.6 m in y, and depth 0.1 m in z.
The default mesh is 200 by 120 by 1 cells, with front and back boundaries set to empty.
The optional fully 3D mesh is 200 by 120 by 20 cells, with the front and back boundaries treated as walls.
Set the tank boundaries as leftWall at x = 0, rightWall at x = 1, bottomWall at y = 0, top at y = 0.6, and frontAndBack at z = 0 and z = 0.1.
On leftWall, rightWall, and bottomWall, set U to noSlip, p_rgh to fixedFluxPressure, and alpha.water to zeroGradient.
On the top boundary, set U to pressureInletOutletVelocity, p_rgh to totalPressure with p0 uniform 0, and alpha.water to inletOutlet with inletValue uniform 0.
For the default 2D mesh, set all fields on frontAndBack to empty.
For the optional 3D mesh, apply the same wall boundary conditions on frontAndBack as on leftWall, rightWall, and bottomWall.
Initialize U to uniform (0 0 0).
Initialize the water surface as a tilted free surface whose water depth varies linearly from 0.25 m at x = 0 to 0.35 m at x = 1.0 m.
Represent the tilted initial interface with a setFieldsDict staircase approximation using one box per x-column, for a total of 200 boxes, each spanning from y = 0 to the local water depth and extending across the full z depth.
Use the setFields utility with boxToCell to set alpha.water to 1 below each local interface height and 0 above it.
Set endTime to 10 s.
Set deltaT to 1e-3 s.
Set adjustTimeStep to yes.
Set maxCo to 0.5.
Set writeInterval to 0.05 s.
Use standard interFoam water and air transport properties, with water density 1000 kg/m3, water kinematic viscosity 1e-6 m2/s, air density 1 kg/m3, and air kinematic viscosity 1.48e-5 m2/s.
Leave fvSchemes and fvSolution to standard interFoam settings, as these are not dictated by the requirement.
